Zero cannot be shown by an objects group with count 0 (rendering unknown), so zero uses short stories with visual none. A better visual: an empty box or plate picture (missing asset).
Educator review of the concrete -> pictorial -> symbolic progression, strategies taught, item difficulty and pass marks (all UNVERIFIED).
en-IN TTS reading of number words and the words 'plus', 'minus', 'times', 'divided by', 'equals' (not heard).

notes: Scope: number 0 only, with its neighbours inside 0-10. Plan covers recognise, count and compare; tracing stays in the existing write step.

Every problem instance (numbers/shape/word) is used once in the lesson, and never equals the lesson's own worked example.

lessons.objective: Subtract within ten without negative results.

introduce.text: Subtracting means taking away. We start with some things and take some away. What is left is the answer.

introduce.text: On a number line, we take away by going back, to the left.

demonstrate.text: Take away 2. These 2 things are crossed out: they go away.

demonstrate.text: Count what is left: 5. So 7 − 2 = 5. The − sign means: take away.
demonstrate.speech: Count what is left: five. So seven minus two equals five. The minus sign means: take away.

demonstrate.text: On the number line, count back 2 steps from 7: 6, 5. We land on 5.

demonstrate.text: Check by adding: start at 5 and count on 2: we get back to 7. So 5 + 2 = 7. Subtracting and adding are partners.

lessons.title: Percent Power
lessons.objective: Calculate a familiar percentage of a quantity.

introduce.text: Percent means out of 100 parts. 100% is the whole set, one whole. We write percent with the sign %.
introduce.speech: Percent means out of one hundred parts. one hundred percent is the whole set, one whole. We write percent with the sign percent.

introduce.text: Some percents are easy fractions. 50% is the same as one half. 25% is the same as one quarter.
introduce.speech: Some percents are easy fractions. fifty percent is the same as one half. twenty-five percent is the same as one quarter.

demonstrate.text: Here is a set of 20 things. The whole set is 100%.
demonstrate.speech: Here is a set of twenty things. The whole set is one hundred percent.

demonstrate.text: Split the whole set into 4 equal groups. Each group has 5. Each group is 25% of the set.
demonstrate.speech: Split the whole set into four equal groups. Each group has five. Each group is twenty-five percent of the set.

demonstrate.text: One group is 25% of the set. So 25% of 20 is 5.
demonstrate.speech: One group is twenty-five percent of the set. So twenty-five percent of twenty is five.

demonstrate.text: Two groups make 50%, which is one half. 50% of 20 is 10.
demonstrate.speech: Two groups make fifty percent, which is one half. fifty percent of twenty is ten.

demonstrate.text: To find 25% of a number, share it into 4 equal groups: 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
demonstrate.speech: To find twenty-five percent of a number, share it into four equal groups: twenty divided by four equals five.
